title: Runtime Energy Ledger Owner Binding and Cross-Column Accepted-Receipt Association Audit
qualified_negative_evidence: Two distinct physical committed columns can legitimately produce accepted commit receipts with identical lineage, origin revision, committed revision, and [t0,t1] tuple.
fmr_accepted_commit_receipt_t carries no logical column or runtime owner identity.
An energy ledger using its own valid prepared handle accepts the real accepted receipt produced by the other physical column when the scalar receipt tuple aliases.
Explicit prepared-handle owner_instance_id therefore prevents foreign prepared-handle use but does not by itself bind accepted physical commit authority to the same logical runtime owner.
The attack is deterministic and O0/O2 identical.
F-KT18 mass-completeness preservation remains PASS; this blocker is a provenance/association defect, not a water-mass defect.

architecture_disposition.reason: Logical column/tile ownership belongs to runtime/coupler composition, while F-KT commit authority remains generic. A private runtime wrapper can bind logical owner identity to the accepted receipt without adding per-column persistent energy state or hidden global identity.

hard_nonclaims: EB-I21 does not remediate the blocker.
EB-I21 does not qualify runtime owner binding.
EB-I21 does not authorize canonical admission.
EB-I21 does not change production or reference source.
next_owner: EB-I21R bounded runtime receipt-owner association remediation plus independent requalification before any F-CI admission
